metadata.title: UK police arrest 5 men near an air base used by US on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act

sources.text:
UK terror plot foiled; Quebec fatal helicopter crash; Robotic surgery
Global National with Dawna Friesen
Monday
25 min
British police have arrested 5 men on suspicion of terrorism, Candice Cole on the potential terror plot that was foiled by a local farmer.
 Dan Spector with the latest on a helicopter crash in Quebec that killed the pilot and three family members.
 Heidi Petracek reports on why environmentalists are critical of the 'Building Canada Strong' act.
 Mike Armstrong reports on the violent weekend in South Africa that saw 27 people killed in two separate mass shootings.
 Katherine Ward on the Toronto hospital network offering cardiac robotic surgery.
 Plus Mike Gazzola speaks with the Canadian doctor leading a double life. Learn more about your ad choices. Visit megaphone.fm/adchoices

(LONDON) — British police announced on Sunday morning that five people were arrested “on suspicion of offenses under the explosives act” close to a major air base hosting U.S. forces in the southwest of England.
“A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident,” Gloucestershire Police said in a statement. “It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offenses under the explosives act.”
The village of Whelford is located around 2 miles from RAF Fairford, which hosts the U.S. Air Force and has since February been serving as a key hub for American operations against Iran — including for heavy bombers like the B-1 Lancer and B-52 Stratofortress.
“The Army’s specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles,” the police statement said.
President Donald Trump said that the suspects in the RAF Fairford counter-terrorism investigation had been under surveillance for a “long time,” telling reporters on Sunday that they were “looking to do big damage” to the U.S. Air Force base there.
“The arrest in the U.K. was fantastic. Working with Britain, it was an amazing job,” Trump told reporters on the tarmac in Illinois while on his way to the Presidents Cup golf tournament in Chicago.
“We had them under investigation,” Trump said. “They were looking to do big damage to our fort.”
The president did not address any potential motive behind the alleged plot.
The U.S. military has used RAF Fairford amid the ongoing war with Iran — though so far no connection to Iran has been confirmed or established by authorities.
“We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” Trump added.
The White House did not respond to additional questions about the investigation.
Local residents were evacuated to a nearby recreation center, with a cordon put in place. “We believe this incident is contained,” police said. “We are working closely with our partners and are enacting the well-rehearsed plans we have in place.”
The U.S. Embassy in the U.K. issued a statement Sunday urging American citizens to “exercise caution and be mindful of personal security” in the country following Sunday’s arrests.
“We remind U.S. citizens that U.K. authorities rate the threat of terrorism in the U.K. as severe. U.S.-associated facilities, gatherings, and organizations may be at heightened risk,” the statement added.
During a press conference later on Sunday, Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone said that police acted after receiving a call about three suspicious vehicles traveling toward the base at 12:45 a.m.
Officers arrested five men, who remain in custody, on suspicion of explosive offenses, Ocone said. Local police, he added, are working closely with counter-terror police on the investigation.
Counter Terrorism Policing confirmed that the five detained men were also arrested “on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act.”
Police said that a 400m cordon was put in place around the suspect’s vehicles while armed forces explosives experts examine them. Around 85 households were also evacuated as a “precaution,” police said.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham posted to social media on Sunday urging people not to speculate about the incident.
“I know today’s incident near RAF Fairford will be deeply concerning for local residents and for many people following developments across the country,” Burnham said.
The prime minister said he was grateful to residents asked to leave their homes while precautionary checks were carried out.
“The safety and security of the public is our first priority, and I want people to know that we will always take every step necessary to protect our communities and keep our country safe,” Burnham said. “The investigation remains ongoing, and I would urge people not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts.”
British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post to X, “We can be reassured that this is being dealt with, and it is exactly why our emergency response teams and Armed Forces are on standby 24/7.”
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood also posted to X thanking the emergency services “for their swift response to the major incident in Gloucestershire this morning and their reassurance that they believe the incident is contained.”
A spokesperson for the U.S. Air Force 501st Combat Support Wing, based at RAF Fairford, told ABC News that the unit “appreciates the swift response and continued support of our local law enforcement partners.”
“The safety and security of our airmen, families, and surrounding communities remains our highest priority,” the spokesperson added. “We remain in close coordination with our U.K. partners to help ensure the safety and security of both our military and local communities.”
Amid reports that U.S. air bases in the U.K. had raised their threat levels, the 48th Fighter Wing — an American unit based at RAF Lakenheath in eastern England — told ABC News in a statement that it was “unable to discuss specific force protection measures” citing “operational security reasons.”
“We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures are implemented or modified. Please be assured that the Tri-Base area (RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall, and RAF Feltwell) remains vigilant and will take appropriate action to ensure the safety and security of U.S. service members, U.S. and U.K. civilians, contractors, and their families,” the statement said.
ABC News’ Rashid Haddou-Riffi, Guy Davies, Lama Hasan, Kevin Shalvey and Jamie Dorrington contributed to this report.

For the past few months, we’ve been told by people with a crystal ball that an attack on UK soil was imminent, and now it’s finally happened. There was an incident at RAF Fairford last night that resulted in 85 homes being evacuated. The media would like you to know this incident was terrifying. So terrifying, in fact, that you should probably get ready for war.
This is an emerging story, but here’s what I’ve managed to piece together so far. Given the media seems to be making this up as it goes along, some of the details are probably gonna change. Needless to say, they have plot holes to fill…
A farmer was driving home in the early hours of the morning and she noticed three white vans blocking the road. No one was inside them. She turned around and spotted a bunch of Middle Eastern-looking boys running off into the woods. Those woods were incredibly dark, but thankfully, she has the eyes of an owl. She was able to work out their ethnicity through the shadow of the trees, despite the fact they were wearing masks.
She called an emergency line that locals had been given for just such a scenario, but no one could be bothered to answer. She called 999 and police came out within ten minutes of her call. When they arrived, they said they’d first been notified nearly an hour ago, but hadn’t bothered doing anything. There were no routine security patrols around the base either. It’s basically the sloppiest security effort since Netanyahu gave standdown orders on October 7.
Luckily for the police, those Middle-Eastern-looking boys were still hanging around 25 minutes later and were arrested under the Explosives Act.
We are told the vans had been driving around the base for hours before they parked up. It’s like they were making their arrival as visible as possible and then they just waited around to be caught. Either it was deliberate or they were just as useless as base security.
Somehow it gets even worse. The vans were parked just six metres from houses, and the company names and telephone numbers on them were fake. Yet it took police around five hours to give evacuation orders. Maybe they knew the vans weren’t a threat, or maybe they’re staggeringly incompetent. I guess it could be both.
Prior to the incident, the base was on its highest alert, and one local said they’d been stopped at gunpoint by Americans. If you didn’t know, this is an American base on our soil, or a “fort” as Trump called it. The US president was giving interviews about the incident shortly after it happened. He said “it worked out great”, which is an odd choice of words, don’t you think?
Trump said the US had been investigating the suspects for a long time. Not sure if he meant “investigating” or actually meant “working with”. All I know is the British are insisting the arrests weren’t intelligence-led and that a farmer basically saved the country.
We are now being told by the war-hungry media it was Iran, Iran, Iran… or maybe Russia, according to one news reader who mumbled something about this is why we need tactical nukes. Yelp.
Now I’m still not clear what these “Iranians” were hoping to achieve. Park vans packed with explosives near a base and blow the whole thing up? Unless they had a nuke, best they’d achieve is damage to a few nearby houses and trees.
If the Iranians wanted to pull this off, they would not hire a bunch of kids to drive in circles for hours around a base that’s on its highest alert and then hide in the woods until they were caught. They would quickly launch drones and disappear.
It seems more likely this was a performance rather than a serious attack. Shortly after it happened, we had a news crew flying above Fairford in a helicopter, showing the location of B1 Stealth Bombers and other sensitive things. If there was a real threat, that’s the last thing they would allow.
Now you have to ask yourself which parties would benefit from this. Israel needs us to join its war, the US needs to keep using Fairford to bomb Iran, and the UK needs to justify its involvement.
Even though we attacked Iran first, they will probably spin it into something like this: “Iran is attacking the UK, even though we are a neutral party. Therefore we have no choice but to get involved”. This would be a terrible legal and moral argument, but it just needs to convince stupid people. We have to make sure stupid people are not taken in by this crap.
Thank you for reading. All of my content will always be freely available, but if you wish to support my work, you can do so at Ko-fi or Patreon. Likes, shares and comments also help massively.
Anyone who's actually been paying attention knows that the Iranians come across as pretty competent (the Russians too). Who do we know is truly incompetent? The list may be quite long, but probably doesn't include many of our "enemies".
Something out of a Mickey Mouse comic! Another Walt Disney Production like the last staged "assassination" of The Drumpf.

A major incident has been declared by Gloucestershire Police after the arrest of five men on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences yesterday (Sunday, September 27).
Police activity is centred around three suspicious vans near RAF Fairford, on the Gloucestershire-Wiltshire border.
The Army's EOD explosives ordnance disposal team used a robot to examine the contents of the three vans.
Eighty-five households in the village of Whelford, close to the entrance to the base, were evacuated and, as of 6.30pm on Sunday, they had been unable to return home.
The RAF base is used primarily by the United States Air Force and has been the USAF's European bomber hub for operations in Iran and the Persian Gulf for months.
Intelligence reports suggest the RAF Fairford has been put on its highest possible alert - FPCON Delta - the Pentagon's top force-protection level.
We will keep you updated with our live blog below. Send us information or pictures if it is safe to do so here.
Key Events
999 caller has only 'partial picture' of incident
Wes Streeting has said that the 999 caller who claimed she raised the alarm only has a "partial picture" of the RAF Fairford.
UK and US 'will always stand together'
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the UK and US will “always stand together against those who hate our freedom and those who wish us harm”, following a suspected terror plot against RAF Fairford.
He told the Labour Party conference: “There is a live police investigation and I can’t provide much further detail than that which is reported.
“But I do want to say that our friendship with America is the closest alliance of any two nations on earth, and we will always stand together against those who hate our freedom and those who wish us harm.
“What we saw yesterday from our security services, our armed forces and our police was just a small glimpse of the extraordinary work they do every day, around the clock and around the world, behind the scenes and without recognition, to keep our country safe.
“To all of them, from all of us, thank you.”
Villager who phoned police only has 'partial picture' of situation says Streeting
Wes Streeting said the member of the public who phoned police about suspicious activity near RAF Fairford has only “a partial picture” of the situation.
The Defence Secretary told Sky News: “Thank you to that member of the public.
“She has done exactly what we would hope that someone in that extraordinary situation would do.
“I’m really grateful to her – I think she acted, by her own admission, quickly and thoughtfully, and she did the right thing.
“With respect, though, she does only have a partial picture.
“And that’s as far as I wish to go this morning but I do want to emphasise my thanks to the police and the security services because their work takes place often unsung, unreported, for good reason.”
Wes Streeting says investigation continues as he thanks members of public
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he is “grateful for the vigilance of the members of the public”, who are thought to have helped alert the emergency services to a suspected terror plot at RAF Fairford.
Speaking on Times Radio on Monday morning, Mr Streeting said the investigation into a suspected terror plot against the Gloucestershire airbase “continues today”.
He added: “We are grateful for the vigilance of the members of the public.
“But I also want to state personally my enormous thanks to our police, our counter-terrorism police, emergency services and the security services for their hard work to defend our base at RAF Fairford. I also want to thank the members of the public who’ve beared (sic) with us.
“We’ve had a number of people evacuated from their homes in the early hours of yesterday morning, there’s a cordon that remains in place and there has been disruption to their lives – and I want to thank them for their forbearance.”
Asked whether the the incident “may have been driven by a hostile foreign state”, Mr Streeting told the broadcaster he did not “want to speculate at this stage of the investigation”.
The minister said: “What I can absolutely assure your listeners of is that, as and when we can, we will report back to the public about these individuals and about the nature of the threat.”
Threat level raised
RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk confirmed it was on Charlie alert, which is the second-highest threat level that can be issued by the US Department of Defence.
The confirmation to PA came amid reports that RAF Fairford has been raised to the highest threat level, Delta.
Police investigate whether Iran linked to suspected RAF base terror plot
Counter terror police are understood to be investigating whether Iran is linked to a suspected terror plot at a military airbase used by US bombers.
The arrests at Fairford come amid heightened concerns around the threat from hostile states to the UK, with Russia and Iran among those that have used proxies to commit crimes on their behalf on British soil.
In March, officials said the number of national security cases involving activity by hostile states including Iran increased 50% in the six months to December 2025.
That same month, after then prime minister Sir Keir Starmer granted permission for “defensive” US action against Iranian missile sites from UK bases, four American bombers landed at RAF Fairford and the US started using British bases for “specific defensive operations”.
The Fairford incident also took place against the backdrop of ongoing war between the US and Iran.
'Looking to do big damage'
A suspected terror plot against an RAF base used by the US Air Force (USAF) was “looking to do big damage”, US President Donald Trump has said.
The police operation near the village of Whelford in Gloucestershire was not intelligence-led – meaning investigators had not known about any potential plot in advance. However, Mr Trump praised the UK police response and suggested authorities already had the suspects under investigation.
“It was fantastic. Working with Britain, it was an amazing job," he said. “We had them under investigation. They, they were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked out great.
“It may have been Scotland Yard, I don’t know. We worked with a lot of them. We had them under view for a long time, and we got them. Thank you.”
Good morning
Good morning and welcome to our second day of live coverage on this incident at RAF Fairford.
We will bring you all the updates below.

Live coverage is now paused
We are pausing our live coverage of the incident at RAF Fairford and will bring you updates as they come in tomorrow.
Several key facts learned from RAF Fairford press conference
Click here to read the eight key facts learned from the RAF Fairford press conference this evening.
Statement from leader of Cotswold District Council
Cotswold District Council leader Mike Evemy issued a statement a short time ago:“Supporting residents affected by the incident in Whelford is our immediate priority. We have opened a rest centre to provide a safe and welcoming place for anyone who has had to leave their home, with council teams on hand to offer help and support.
“We are working closely with the emergency services and our partners as the situation continues, and I want to thank everyone involved for their hard work, as well as residents for their patience and cooperation.
“We know this will be an unsettling time for many people and we will continue to support our residents for as long as we are needed. In the meantime, I would encourage everyone to follow official advice."
Police believe incident is 'contained'
Temporary Chief Constable Maggie Blyth said that while she couldn't go into detail, she "can give reassurance that we believe the matter to be contained".
Arrests were made by Gloucestershire Police
Temporary Chief Constable of Gloucestershire Police Maggie Blyth confirmed the force’s officers arrested the five men near RAF Fairford.
She said she would leave any declaration of a “terrorist incident” in Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP)’s hands as it was leading the investigation.
Asked if Gloucestershire Police had been preparing for an incident like this given the large scale of Fairford base, she told a press conference, joined by representatives from the fire service and district council: “The purpose of us standing here together is, as different agencies, we prepare for these sorts of major incidents all of the time, and we’re very well prepared, as we have been in the last day, to do this, and this is a normal response for us.”
No declaration of a terrorist incident has been made by CTP.
Residents unable to return home
The Army’s ordnance disposal unit is still examining the vehicles near RAF Fairford and a cordon remains in place around them, police have said.
Temporary Chief Constable Maggie Blyth, of Gloucestershire Police, told reporters that 85 households are still unable to return home.
She said: “Counter-terrorism police are leading the investigation which means I’m unable to provide any additional information about this, but we’ve asked you here this afternoon, as senior leaders of agencies in Gloucestershire, as we wanted to provide reassurance to our local communities.
“These arrests will no doubt have caused some shock and anxiety and we want those living locally to RAF Fairford and across Gloucestershire to be sure and to know that, as agencies, we are working closely together to support them.”
She added: “We are co-ordinating our plans through the Local Resilience Forum as local agencies – that is our normal procedures for multi-agency planning… to ensure that people are looked after and have the information that they need.
“You will appreciate this is a fast-moving situation and all agencies across Gloucestershire are actively working to respond to our communities’ needs and continue to provide information to our communities on a regular basis, we will also continue to assist counter-terrorism policing with their investigation and liaise with other national partners.”
PCC for Gloucestershire comments on 'fast-moving situation'
Police and Crime Commissioner for Gloucestershire Chris Nelson said:
“I have refrained from commenting until now, as the Constabulary leads on all operational matters, and it has needed time to establish all the key facts in a fast-moving situation. I’d like to begin by thanking the residents of Whelford and Fairford for their understanding whilst policing and the armed forces have been dealing with this incident.
“Strong communities, like those in the Cotswolds are what helps keep communities safe and make them more resilient.
“I also want to pay tribute to the comprehensive emergency service and local council response, following well understood major incident and contingency plans. It demonstrates the variety of policing tasks required by Gloucestershire Constabulary and the challenges that we face in keeping residents of the County safe.
“As Police and Crime Commissioner and your elected representative on policing matters, my focus is always on local residents. I will work hard to ensure residents are kept updated about when they can safely return to their homes, and what additional reassurance can be provided to them in the weeks and months ahead, and I will be speaking to the Government about how Gloucestershire Constabulary can be assisted in that important task.”
Everything we know so far
Click here to read everything that we know so far and a timeline of events throughout today.
Streeting says security services owed 'huge debt of thanks'
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting praised the “exemplary response” from the security services to the RAFFairford incident.
Speaking at a Labour Party conference fringe event in Liverpool, he said it was “an example of what they do day in, day out, at all hours and all across the world, to keep us safe, so often going unnoticed and unsung, but we are glad that they do and we are glad that they are there to defend us.
He added: “We owe them a huge debt of thanks for today and what they do for us every day, every year.”
US military 'working closely with UK counterparts'
Responding to the incident near RAF Fairford, a spokesperson for the US military said: “We are working closely with our UK counterparts to monitor this situation, minimise impacts and ensure the safety of US personnel, their families, and the local community.”
Defence Secretary in contact with American counterpart
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he would not comment on a live operation but he had been in contact with Pete Hegseth, his opposite number in the US.
Speaking at a fringe event at Labour conference, he said: “I don’t think it will come as a surprise to anyone that, given the importance of Fairford, not just to the United Kingdom but to the United States, we’ve been working closely with our American friends, and I’ve been in touch during the course of today with my counterpart Pete Hegseth.”
Asked if there was any Iranian involvement, he said: “I’m not going to comment on the underlying motivations of those who’ve been arrested today, or indeed the, sort of, the genesis of their activity, I think it’s far too early to comment or speculate, and it would be irresponsible for me to do so.”
Prime Minister thanks emergency services and residents who evacuated their homes
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "I know today's incident near RAF Fairford will be deeply concerning for local residents and for many people following developments across the country.
"My thanks go to Gloucestershire Police, Counter Terrorism Policing, our Armed Forces and all those working to keep the public safe.
" I am especially grateful to those residents who have been asked to leave their homes while precautionary checks are carried out.
"The safety and security of the public is our first priority, and I want people to know that we will always take every step necessary to protect our communities and keep our country safe.
"The investigation remains ongoing, and I would urge people not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts."
Resident said he 'saw men being held by police'
Jeff, one of the local people who was evacuated, told the BBC: "I heard shouting outside at about 02:00 BST. [I] looked out the window and saw men were being held by police outside the house.
"They were armed. It was surreal."
Jeff said he got to the leisure centre a few hours later and the centre pauid for tea, coffee and bacon sandwiches.
"We've been asked if we have anywhere to stay overnight. The whole village is here. There's about 60 houses in the village."
Donald Trump's response to incident
The American president has suggested that the men arrested were under investigation, seemingly contradicting what has been said by police earlier today.
Donald Trump said: "Working with Britain, it was an amazing job. We had them under investigation.
"They were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked out great and we got them."
Suspects could be in custody for two weeks without charge
Suspects arrested under the Terrorism Act 2000 can be detained for up to 14 days without charge, compared to the 24-hour limit for standard arrests without an extension application.
Timeline of United States Air Force at RAF Fairford
It has been six months since the United States Air Force (USAF) started sending US bomber jets to the base back in March as the US-Iran conflice began.
The USAF has used the airbase prior to this, an agreement was reached in 1948 that the American military could use the base during the Cold War, however the use of the RAF base within the last six months has left residents feeling conflicted.
Click here to read about the history of the RAF base and a timeline of the last six months.
Local councillor calls incident 'destabilising'
People evacuated from their homes near RAF Fairford may have to stay overnight as the emergency services make the scene safe, a local councillor has said, as he described the incident as “destabilising”.
Gloucestershire County Councillor Paul Hodgkinson told the Press Association the incident is “very different”.
“We’re not used to something where there’s a potential terrorist incident,” Mr Hodgkinson said.
“It’s not something we’ve encountered in Gloucestershire before in recent times, and so it is worrying.
“I mean, clearly it’s destabilising. Although that’s the whole point of terrorism, isn’t it? Is to destabilise. And clearly, we don’t know yet exactly what the circumstances are.”
He said it is possible residents will have to stay away from their homes overnight.
Asked whether there had been any more preparations to protect people living near Fairford amid global conflicts, Mr Hodgkinson said: “We are in a more heightened state of awareness around these things.”
'Preparation of terrorist act'
The five men detained near RAF Fairford have been further arrested on suspicion of the preparation of a terrorist act, the Metropolitan Police said.
A Met statement said: “Counter Terrorism Policing can now confirm they are leading an investigation into an incident which took place overnight near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire.
“At around 12.45am today (Sunday 27 September), police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the air base.
“Armed officers responded and five men were arrested in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. They were further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act, contrary to section 5 of the Terrorism Act.”
Counter Terrorism Policing Senior National Coordinator, Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said: “We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody. As you would expect we are working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident.
“We continue to work with Gloucestershire Police to keep the community safe as we work to gather evidence from the scene. A 400m cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while the Army’s Explosive Ordinance Disposal unit conduct examinations. As a precaution, around 85 households have been evacuated whilst these examinations take place.”
Pictures of 'detained men'
Images have been circulating on social media which appears to show five topless men sitting on the ground having been detained by armed police.
Suspicious vans
This image shows how close the suspicious vans currently are to military vans. A bomb disposal robot is travelling between the two points.
Five men arrested
Police have confirmed that five men have been arrested under the Explosives Act. Police were called at around 12.45am to reports of three suspicious vehicles heading towards RAF Fairford. Armed police were quickly on the scene. 85 households were asked to evacuate. Work is ongoing to establish the full nature of the incident with Gloucestershire Police working with Counter Terrorism Police.
